title: The Input Manager
description: Discover Unity's built-in input system, the Input Manager, and how it maps keys, buttons, and axes to actions.

slides.title: How Unity Sees Your Controls 🎮
slides.content:
# The Input Manager

Unity comes with a classic **Input Manager** that lets you define **Axes** (floating values) and **Buttons** (true/false). It's configured in **Edit → Project Settings → Input Manager**.

You don't have to hardcode "W", "UpArrow", etc. Instead you use abstract names like "Horizontal" and "Fire1", and Unity maps them to multiple physical keys or joystick axes.

This makes your game automatically support keyboard, gamepad, and more.

quizData.question: What is the main advantage of using the Input Manager over hardcoding specific keys?

options.text: It allows players to remap controls and supports multiple input devices
It automatically creates buttons on screen

quizData.explanation: The Input Manager abstracts input actions from physical keys, enabling cross-device support and remapping.

slides.title: Built-in Axes & Buttons 📜
slides.content:
# Default Setup

When you create a new project, the Input Manager already contains:
- **Horizontal** – left/right (A/D, Left/Right Arrow, gamepad left stick X).
- **Vertical** – up/down (W/S, Up/Down Arrow, gamepad left stick Y).
- **Fire1**, **Fire2**, **Fire3** – mouse buttons and Ctrl/Alt/Shift.
- **Jump** – Space bar.
- **Mouse X**, **Mouse Y** – mouse movement delta.
- **Submit**, **Cancel** – for UI.

You can add custom axes by increasing the **Size** field and configuring new entries.

quizData.question: Which predefined axis is typically used for left/right movement?
quizData.explanation: Horizontal maps to A/D and left/right arrows by default.

slides.title: Axis Properties ⚙️
slides.content:
# Configuring an Axis

Each axis entry has:
- **Name** – the string you use in code (e.g., "Horizontal").
- **Negative Button** / **Positive Button** – keys (e.g., "left", "a").
- **Alt Negative/Positive** – alternative keys (e.g., joystick button).
- **Gravity** – how fast the axis returns to zero when no input.
- **Sensitivity** – how fast it reaches +1 or -1.
- **Snap** – if true, it jumps to zero when opposite direction pressed.
- **Type** – Key/Mouse button, Mouse movement, Joystick Axis, etc.
- **Axis** – for joysticks: X axis, Y axis, 3rd axis…
- **Joy Num** – which joystick.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## The New Input System

Unity also offers a **new Input System** package (more powerful, event-driven). For beginners, the classic Input Manager is simpler. We'll stick with it, but know that for commercial projects you may switch later.
